answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy makes identity expensive instead of free: every agent must lock a stake before it can transact, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes, and a caught cheat forfeits its bond. Trust then enters through one narrow inlet - a history of completed work - not through self-declared claims. Honest agents gossip fraud reports peer to peer, like a raven carrying the news, so one exposed fake poisons all its clones at once. A saffron-grade audit trail, every deal signed and timestamped, makes faking history cost more than a single scam can earn.
